title: Convexity & Optimization Intuition
interviewAnswer: A convex objective has no bad local minima: any local minimum is global. Deep networks are non-convex, so optimization relies on practical gradient methods rather than global-optimum guarantees.
why: Convexity explains why some optimization problems are globally well-behaved while deep-network training is not.
intuition: A convex bowl has no deceptive local valleys: the line segment between two points stays above the function, and any local minimum is global.
deepDive: For differentiable convex f, f(y)≥f(x)+∇f(x)ᵀ(y-x). Strong convexity gives curvature bounds and faster guarantees. Linear/logistic regression with suitable losses can be convex in parameters, while neural networks are highly non-convex. Non-convex does not mean impossible; gradient methods can still find useful solutions in overparameterized landscapes.
workedExample: Least-squares linear regression has a convex quadratic objective; changing initialization does not create distinct bad local minima in the same way a deep network can.
commonMistakes: Saying convex functions are always easy regardless of conditioning/scale.
Assuming non-convex training necessarily gets stuck in poor local minima.
production: Convex baselines are valuable for reliability and debugging; if a complex model barely beats one, production complexity may not be justified.
